tasks.short: Match supplier invoices to orders and receipts, then record them in AFAS.

today.trigger: A supplier invoice arrives in Outlook or a staffing agency portal.
steps: Find the order, agreed price and receipt confirmation in the available records.
Compare quantities, rates, VAT and totals; check for duplicate invoices.
Ask the relevant site or budget holder about missing receipts or differences.
Record the invoice and supporting documents in AFAS for approval.
drudgery: Finding the same order reference across documents.
today.time_sinks: Missing order references and receipt evidence, especially when agency invoices combine multiple sites and weeks.

lenses.faster: Read structured invoices directly and extract fields from PDFs when needed. Rules compare them with approved orders and receipts, removing most searching and rekeying.
lenses.autonomous: Invoice arrival starts duplicate checks, matching and recording for transactions that meet approved rules. Missing receipts, unfamiliar suppliers and differences enter an exception queue.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency invoice line against approved hours and contracted rates, including site and week. Give the Controller a daily view of received services awaiting invoices.
lenses.joy: Stop copying lines and reopening attachments. Spend time resolving real supplier differences and helping sites provide better evidence.
lenses.options: For an unmatched line, show possible orders with supporting references. Offer partial matching or requesting a corrected invoice without inventing a receipt.
lenses.altitude: Own the matching rules, exception categories and supplier data quality. Review why invoices need intervention and remove recurring causes.
reach: Prepare the Accountant's received-but-not-invoiced schedule.
Support site buyers with order and receipt quality.
Provide agency invoice discrepancy evidence to Payroll and HR.

tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a plausible match hides a delivery dispute, unauthorised purchase or unusual agency charge.
tasks.pattern_why: Use an LLM only to turn unstructured documents into candidate fields with source references. Deterministic rules perform matching, arithmetic and posting; structured invoices bypass the model.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice enters the designated mailbox or an authorised portal import.
steps: Preserve the original invoice and assign a unique processing identifier.
Read structured fields or extract candidate fields with references to the original document.
Validate supplier, duplicate status, totals, approved order and receipt evidence.
Record qualifying invoices within approved tolerances and route exceptions to the bookkeeper.
Retain the match evidence and update processing status after AFAS confirms the result.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper resolves exceptions; the budget holder confirms disputed receipt or price differences. Supplier bank changes and payment release require separate approval.
systems: Proposed document extraction and validation service
data_needed: Supplier master and invoice history
Approved orders and receipt confirmations
Approved agency hours and contracted rates
Controller-approved matching tolerances
Available AFAS modules, version and integration permissions
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice dossier and a restricted SharePoint processing register containing source references, rule version, exceptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports matching electronic invoice lines against receipts or commitments, with configurable tolerances and matching rules; Noordhaven's licensed configuration needs verification.
The proposed 65% reduction in human handling and 1.8-fold end-to-end speedup are untested pilot estimates.

risks: An order match alone does not prove that goods or services were received.
PDF extraction can misread rates, credits or VAT; model confidence alone cannot authorise posting.
Invoice text could contain malicious instructions; treat documents as data and restrict available actions.
Agency invoice evidence can contain personal data; limit access and model inputs under AVG/GDPR.
research_questions: What proportion of invoices already has structured fields, approved order references and receipt evidence?
Which AFAS matching functions are licensed and already configured?
Can all three agencies supply invoice lines and approved hours with stable identifiers?
Does a pilot reduce handling and elapsed time without increasing incorrect matches or audit adjustments?

tasks.short: Check debits, credits and totals in AFAS and the supporting Excel schedules.

today.trigger: Daily transactions or a supporting schedule need checking before completion.
steps: Open the relevant AFAS transactions and supporting Excel schedule.
Check debit and credit signs, totals and account references.
Compare schedule totals with AFAS balances and investigate differences.
Complete the permitted entries and retain the checked schedule.
drudgery: Recalculating totals already available in AFAS.
Checking copied formulas and reversed signs.
today.time_sinks: Finding which workbook version is current and tracing differences between supporting schedules and AFAS.

lenses.faster: Use AFAS totals and validated data connections instead of copying balances into Excel. Automatic checks flag unbalanced entries, missing dimensions and formula errors.
lenses.autonomous: A completed transaction or refreshed schedule triggers the checks. Standard approved calculations run automatically and failures appear in a work queue.
lenses.ambitious: Check every supporting schedule each day rather than discovering broken formulas during close. Make every reported total traceable to its transactions.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated addition and formula repair. Keep the useful work of explaining unusual balances.
lenses.options: Show alternative views by account, site and period without rebuilding workbooks. Let the bookkeeper trace each difference to its source.
lenses.altitude: Maintain calculation templates and control checks. Retire spreadsheets that duplicate AFAS without adding evidence or analysis.
reach: Maintain the Accountant's standard supporting schedules.
Check the arithmetic and source totals of Controller reporting packs.
Help the FP&A Analyst reconcile actuals to forecast inputs.

tasks.human_edge: A balanced entry can still be wrong; the bookkeeper understands its business meaning and challenges unusual movements.
tasks.pattern_why: Arithmetic, balance checks and approved account mappings are explicit and testable. Existing AFAS functions and small validated routines are sufficient; a model should not calculate ledger amounts.

in_practice.trigger: An AFAS transaction completes or an approved supporting schedule refreshes.
steps: Read transaction balances and schedule inputs with their period and extraction timestamp.
Apply approved sign conventions, formulas and account mappings.
Check debit-credit balance, completeness and agreement to AFAS.
Complete approved routine processing and place failed checks in an exception queue.
Publish the checked schedule with links to underlying transactions.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper handles failed checks; the Accountant approves new journal logic and material corrections before posting.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and site dimensions
Approved formulas and journal templates
Current AFAS balances and transaction identifiers
Open accounting periods and approval limits
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS transaction history and a SharePoint schedule register recording input timestamps, calculation versions and failed checks.

evidence.claim: AFAS processes completed journal transactions into the general ledger and checks that debit and credit totals balance when a journal is changed.
The proposed 35% handling reduction and 1.5-fold speedup depend on residual spreadsheet work; existing AFAS automation may leave little additional saving.

risks: Correct arithmetic can conceal an incorrect account, VAT code or accounting period.
Using a nightly Power BI extract for current transaction controls can create false differences.
Changing a shared formula can affect many schedules at once.
Automating checks already performed by AFAS adds maintenance without saving time.
research_questions: How much of the stated time is manual checking beyond controls AFAS already performs?
Which Excel schedules add necessary evidence, and which merely duplicate ledger totals?
Can schedules read current AFAS data without manual exports?
Do automated checks detect known historical errors while keeping false alerts manageable?

tasks.short: Code transactions to the right accounts and sites, then keep the financial records complete.

today.trigger: An invoice, credit note or other transaction requires financial classification.
steps: Read the source document and identify the business purpose.
Select the ledger account, VAT code, site and accounting period.
Record the transaction in AFAS with its supporting evidence.
Check summaries and refer unfamiliar treatments to the Accountant.
drudgery: Looking up how similar transactions were coded.
today.time_sinks: Ambiguous descriptions, inconsistent historical coding and transactions spanning several sites or accounting periods.

lenses.faster: Approved supplier and transaction rules fill routine codes. For unfamiliar documents, AI proposes codes with source passages and relevant approved examples.
lenses.autonomous: Known transactions with complete evidence follow approved coding rules automatically. Unfamiliar treatment, mixed VAT or uncertain site allocation requires review.
lenses.ambitious: Check coding consistency across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo continuously. Give FP&A more reliable site costs before the month-end rush.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive account lookups and description typing. Keep investigating costs and improving the quality of financial records.
lenses.options: Show plausible coding alternatives and explain what evidence distinguishes them. Flag splitting costs across sites or periods for review.
lenses.altitude: Maintain a coding guide and monitor where proposed codes are corrected. Turn approved recurring decisions into explicit rules.
reach: Support the Accountant with transaction classification evidence.
Maintain site cost coding quality for FP&A.
Prepare recurring coding issues for the Controller's control review.

tasks.human_edge: Understand the substance of a transaction, especially capital expenditure, disputed charges and unusual VAT treatment.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured descriptions can become structured coding proposals. Approved mappings, permitted values and posting checks remain deterministic, with uncertain accounting treatment reviewed by a person.

in_practice.trigger: A validated source transaction enters the coding queue.
steps: Apply approved supplier and transaction mappings before using a model.
For unmatched documents, propose permitted codes and cite the supporting text.
Validate account, VAT code, site, period and any allocation against approved rules.
Post established rule-based cases and route all uncertain proposals for review.
Record accepted and corrected codes without automatically changing the approved rules.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper reviews uncertain coding; the Accountant decides unfamiliar VAT, capitalisation and period treatment. New rules require approval.
data_needed: Approved chart of accounts and coding guide
Supplier mappings and site dimensions
Reviewed examples rather than unchecked historical postings
Source documents and open accounting periods
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS transaction dossier and a restricted classification register with source passages, proposed codes, rule versions and reviewer changes.

evidence.claim: AFAS electronic invoice matching rules can assign ledger accounts, VAT groups and financial dimensions from specified search criteria.
Source-based coding proposals are plausible, but the proposed 55% handling reduction and 1.7-fold speedup are untested at Noordhaven.

risks: Historical coding errors can be repeated at scale.
A supplier default may be wrong for an unusual purchase from that supplier.
A fluent explanation does not establish correct Dutch VAT treatment.
Sensitive employee details may appear in invoices and must be minimised before model processing.
research_questions: What percentage of transactions follows stable, approved coding rules?
Are historical examples accurate enough to use as reference material?
Can reviewers validate proposals faster than they currently code transactions?
Does a trial improve site coding completeness without increasing later reclassifications?

tasks.short: Bring approved journal details into AFAS and check that every entry arrived once.

today.trigger: An approved external journal or supporting file is ready for the ledger.
steps: Obtain the approved journal or export and identify its accounting period.
Map external fields to AFAS accounts, sites and journal fields.
Import or enter the residual transactions that are not already integrated.
Compare record counts and totals and retain evidence of completion.
systems: Staffing agency portals where they supply relevant files
drudgery: Checking whether an import has already run.
today.time_sinks: Inconsistent external file layouts and proving that an import was complete without duplicating entries.

lenses.faster: Replace recurring file manipulation with validated mappings and control totals. AFAS-native transactions already reach the ledger automatically and should require no extra transfer.
lenses.autonomous: Arrival of an approved file triggers validation and import. Unknown layouts, invalid codes and closed periods stop processing and create an exception.
lenses.ambitious: Bring remaining external feeds into the ledger earlier and maintain a complete source-to-ledger trail. Reduce late journals that delay close and distort forecast actuals.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive file formatting and row counting. Keep investigating missing or inconsistent source data.
lenses.options: Preview the same approved journal by account, site and period before import. Show the exact records causing validation failure.
lenses.altitude: Own the external feed catalogue, mappings and completion controls. Measure late, rejected and duplicated feeds.
reach: Maintain the Accountant's recurring journal import process.
Support the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst with payroll-to-finance interface checks.
Provide feed completeness evidence for the Controller's close checklist.

tasks.human_edge: Decide whether source approval is sufficient and recognise when a changed file reflects a changed business process.
tasks.pattern_why: Field mapping, control totals and duplicate prevention are explicit rules. Use native integration where available and a validated import routine for residual external sources.

in_practice.trigger: An approved source batch becomes available through an authorised export or integration.
steps: Check source approval, batch identifier, layout version and accounting period.
Map fields using the approved mapping and validate codes, counts and debit-credit totals.
Import once and retain the source batch identifier against the resulting entries.
Reconcile source totals with AFAS acknowledgements and resulting ledger entries.
Stop incomplete or ambiguous runs and route them for investigation before retrying.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant approves new mappings and journal logic. The bookkeeper handles failed imports; approved routine batches require no additional approval per row.
data_needed: Approved source files and batch identifiers
Account and site mapping tables
Expected record counts and control totals
AFAS import permissions and available integration methods
Open accounting periods
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS import and journal history plus a SharePoint batch register linking source files, totals, mapping versions and acknowledgements.

evidence.claim: AFAS automatically processes completed financial transactions into the ledger; manual transfer is therefore a residual external-file task, not a necessary AFAS step.
AFAS Payroll can generate and transfer payroll journals to Profit Financieel after payroll approval.
The 75% handling reduction and threefold speedup assume material residual file work; they are untested estimates.

risks: Retries after an unclear import result can create duplicate journals.
A balanced batch can still omit transactions.
Changed source layouts can silently shift account or site mappings.
Savings overlap with coding and calculation tasks if the same file work is counted more than once.
research_questions: Which journal transfers still happen manually outside native AFAS integration?
Do external files contain stable batch identifiers and reliable control totals?
Can the integration confirm partial success and prevent duplicate retries?
How much of the 54.2-hour baseline duplicates time allocated to other listed tasks?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, supplier and customer records, and explain the differences.

today.trigger: A bank statement arrives, a supplier statement is received or a reconciliation is due.
steps: Collect Rabobank transactions, AFAS balances and relevant statements.
Match payments, invoices, credits and opening balances.
Investigate unmatched amounts using documents and correspondence.
Prepare proposed corrections and report unresolved differences.
drudgery: Rewriting the same explanations for open differences.
today.time_sinks: Combined payments, partial settlements, missing credit notes and differences caused by timing.

lenses.faster: Let AFAS clear recognised bank transactions and use rules to compare remaining records. AI assembles evidence and drafts explanations for unresolved differences.
lenses.autonomous: A statement import starts matching and prepares the reconciliation pack. Proposed corrections and final reconciliation sign-off remain gated.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile key accounts daily and show aged differences with owners. Give the Controller earlier warning of cash allocation and close problems.
lenses.joy: Remove line-by-line searching and repeated explanation writing. Keep solving awkward cases with customers, suppliers and colleagues.
lenses.options: Show alternative payment allocations and distinguish timing differences from likely errors. Provide evidence for each option.
lenses.altitude: Manage reconciliation coverage, unresolved-item age and recurring failure causes. Improve references and upstream processes.
reach: Prepare balance-sheet reconciliation packs for the Accountant.
Support the Credit and Collections Officer with payment allocation evidence.
Supply the Controller with aged reconciliation exceptions.

tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an accounting error from a commercial dispute, fraud concern or legitimate timing difference.
tasks.pattern_why: Investigation spans bank records, ledger entries and correspondence. Rules perform matching; an agent prepares an evidence pack, while a person approves corrections and reconciliation conclusions.

in_practice.trigger: A new bank or supplier statement arrives, or a scheduled reconciliation is due.
steps: Capture statement balances, ledger balances and their effective dates.
Run approved matching rules and verify opening balance plus movements equals closing balance.
Investigate remaining differences using permitted read-only records.
Prepare proposed allocations or corrections with evidence and unresolved-item owners.
Obtain approval, apply authorised corrections and regenerate the reconciliation.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves ambiguous allocations and signs the prepared reconciliation within their authority. The Accountant approves material correcting journals; write-offs go to the authorised approver.
data_needed: Bank and supplier statements
AFAS open items and ledger movements
Remittance advice and relevant correspondence
Matching rules and correction approval limits
Effective dates and source timestamps
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS clearing and journal history and a SharePoint reconciliation pack containing evidence, unresolved items, proposed corrections and sign-off.

evidence.claim: AFAS can automatically import bank statements and match recognised lines to open items or ledger accounts when configured.
An assistant assembling reconciliation evidence is plausible; the 55% handling reduction and 1.6-fold speedup remain pilot hypotheses.

risks: Matching equal amounts can allocate a payment to the wrong invoice.
Different effective dates can create misleading discrepancies.
Automatic write-offs could hide fraud or unresolved disputes.
Correspondence may contain personal or bank data that should not enter unrestricted model services.
research_questions: What match rate does the existing AFAS bank configuration already achieve?
Can the assistant resolve known combined and partial payments using reliable evidence?
Which reconciliation delays arise from investigation rather than waiting for third parties?
Does a pilot reduce aged differences without increasing wrong allocations or audit corrections?

tasks.short: Prepare payroll checks and finance postings for the Payroll Specialist.

today.trigger: Approved payroll inputs or a payroll run are ready for finance support.
steps: Collect approved variable-pay inputs and identify missing or inconsistent records.
Check totals and site allocations against the agreed payroll control process.
Send the exceptions and supporting evidence to the Payroll Specialist.
After payroll approval, check the payroll journal and payment control totals in finance.
today.time_sinks: Late shift and overtime inputs, retrospective corrections and distinguishing employee payroll from agency invoices.

lenses.faster: Generate checks from approved AFAS inputs and reuse approved account and site mappings. Remove duplicate exports and manual comparison of payroll control totals.
lenses.autonomous: Approved inputs trigger an exception report; payroll approval triggers native journal transfer. The Payroll Specialist retains approval of each payroll run.
lenses.ambitious: Check variable-pay completeness before the payroll deadline at all three sites. Provide reconciled labour costs for the forecast without exposing employee detail.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated spreadsheet comparisons and deadline chasing. Keep helping colleagues resolve genuine pay discrepancies accurately.
lenses.options: Show variance explanations by site and pay component. Offer correction routes for Payroll to assess, rather than letting a model choose an employee's entitlement.
lenses.altitude: Own the finance-side payroll reconciliation and input completeness controls. Improve the handoff between sites, Payroll and Finance.
reach: Prepare routine completeness checks for the Payroll Specialist.
Maintain labour-cost reconciliation schedules for the Accountant.
Provide aggregated labour-cost actuals and approved commitments to FP&A.

tasks.human_edge: Pay affects people's livelihoods; CAO interpretation, unusual entitlements and sensitive employee cases require Payroll expertise.
tasks.pattern_why: Approved payroll calculations, control totals and journal mappings belong in AFAS and explicit rules. AI may help build checks, but should not decide CAO entitlements or calculate payroll independently.

in_practice.trigger: Approved variable-pay inputs become available or a payroll run reaches its review stage.
steps: Read only authorised input fields and check completeness against expected submissions.
Apply Payroll-approved checks for duplicates, unusual changes and site allocations.
Prepare an exception pack without medical details or unnecessary employee identifiers.
Have the Payroll Specialist resolve exceptions and approve the payroll run.
Use native journal transfer and reconcile finance totals to the approved payroll and payment totals.
in_practice.human_gate: The Payroll Specialist approves inputs, CAO treatment and each run. Bank payment release remains with authorised signatories, separate from preparation.
data_needed: Approved variable-pay inputs
Payroll Specialist-approved rules for both applicable CAOs
Pay component, account and site mappings
Prior-period and current-run control totals
Role-based access and payroll approval status
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS payroll approval and journal history, plus a restricted payroll-finance control register with reconciliations and approver identities.

evidence.claim: AFAS can automatically journal an approved payroll run and transfer its journal to Profit Financieel.
Changes to employee personal-data processing arrangements and monitoring provisions can require works council consent.
Employment and worker-management AI uses require assessment against the AI Act's relevant risk categories; the classification depends on the intended use.
The 40% handling reduction and 1.3-fold speedup are untested estimates for the bookkeeper's support work.

risks: CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and the warehouse CAO require distinct approved rules; a model must not infer pay entitlements.
Agency workers' invoices must not be treated as Noordhaven employee payroll.
AVG/GDPR requires restricted access and minimum necessary fields; Wet verbetering poortwachter casework and medical details stay outside this finance workflow.
Review OR requirements when changing employee-data arrangements; assess EU AI Act classification if AI begins influencing employment decisions or monitoring workers.
research_questions: What payroll support do bookkeepers actually perform, and what belongs solely to the Payroll Specialist?
Are variable-pay inputs approved and available in structured form before the deadline?
Are both CAOs and retrospective corrections correctly configured in AFAS?
Can the pilot reduce finance handling without exposing unnecessary employee data or delaying payroll approval?

tasks.short: Prepare customer invoices and statements from approved services and agreed rates.

today.trigger: Approved transport or warehouse service records become billable, or customer statements are due.
steps: Obtain approved service quantities and the applicable customer rate agreement.
Calculate charges, agreed surcharges and VAT using established procedures.
Prepare the invoice or account statement and check references and totals.
Issue the document through the approved channel and record it in AFAS.
drudgery: Copying service quantities into billing files.
today.time_sinks: Missing service approval, customer-specific references and rate agreements that are difficult to translate into billing rules.

lenses.faster: Use approved service records and versioned rate rules to generate bills and statements. Remove repeated calculation, document assembly and ledger re-entry.
lenses.autonomous: A service approval or agreed billing date triggers invoice generation. Complete routine invoices issue automatically; missing evidence and nonstandard charges require review.
lenses.ambitious: Bill promptly after confirmed service delivery and attach evidence customers need to approve payment. Track approved services that remain unbilled to improve close and DSO.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive statement preparation and customer-reference typing. Keep resolving genuine billing questions with operations and customers.
lenses.options: Preview permitted invoice groupings by order, site or billing period. Compare them against the customer's agreed format before changing the setup.
lenses.altitude: Maintain billing rules and monitor missing evidence, rejected invoices and unbilled services. Fix upstream causes of delayed cash collection.
reach: Prepare unbilled-service schedules for the Accountant.
Support the Credit and Collections Officer with invoice delivery and dispute evidence.
Provide billing completeness and timing data to FP&A.

tasks.human_edge: Understand commercial agreements and recognise charges that are arithmetically correct but unsupported or likely to be disputed.
tasks.pattern_why: Approved quantities, agreed rates and billing formats can be expressed as rules. Use a model only to propose extraction from contract text, with a person approving the resulting rate rules before use.

in_practice.trigger: An approved service record becomes billable or a configured billing cycle starts.
steps: Validate service approval, customer identity and a unique billable-event reference.
Apply the approved rate version, surcharge rules and VAT treatment.
Check required invoice fields, customer references, totals and duplicate status.
Issue qualifying invoices through the agreed channel and create the AFAS receivable.
Record delivery status and route missing data, rejected delivery and nonstandard charges for review.
in_practice.human_gate: Commercial owners approve rate agreements and operations confirms service delivery. The bookkeeper reviews exceptions; credit notes and disputed charges follow existing authority limits.
systems: Outlook or an agreed invoicing channel
data_needed: Confirmed service quantities and unique references
Approved customer rate and surcharge tables with effective dates
Customer invoice requirements and delivery contacts
Approved VAT treatment
Prior invoices, credits and open items
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice dossier and a billing register linking service evidence, rate version, validation outcome and delivery status.

evidence.claim: AFAS can generate financial sales transactions from invoicing modules or an integrated industry application; the applicable billing module and source connection need verification.
Dutch invoice retention generally requires seven years, with ten-year requirements for specified categories such as immovable-property invoices.
The 60% handling reduction and 1.8-fold speedup assume reliable service records and rate rules; neither has been measured.

risks: The company description does not identify the operational source of billable transport and warehouse services.
Incorrect rate effective dates or surcharge rules can affect many customer invoices.
Unsupported service evidence can increase disputes even when invoices are generated faster.
Invoice, delivery and credit records must remain traceable and retained under the applicable fiscal rules.
research_questions: Where are completed transport and warehouse services recorded and approved?
Which AFAS billing module or external billing integration is currently used?
What share of customer agreements can be represented as stable, approved rate rules?
Does earlier billing reduce rejection rates and DSO, or merely move the same approval delay upstream?

tasks.short: Prepare purchase orders and employee expense reports for approval.

today.trigger: A site requests a purchase or an employee submits an expense claim.
steps: Collect the purchase request, quote or receipt and the business purpose.
Check supplier or employee details, site allocation and required evidence.
Prepare the order or expense report against the applicable policy.
Route it to the authorised approver and record the approved result.
drudgery: Returning incomplete submissions and chasing approvals.
today.time_sinks: Unclear business purposes, missing receipts and approval routing across three sites.

lenses.faster: Extract request and receipt details, check policy rules and prepare a complete approval pack. Remove repeated typing and manual searches for the correct approver.
lenses.autonomous: Submission triggers completeness checks, draft preparation and routing. A purchase commitment or reimbursement is created only after the authorised approval.
lenses.ambitious: Give sites a consistent request process and track approved commitments before invoices arrive. Detect recurring missing receipts and expense-policy confusion.
lenses.joy: Remove formatting and routine approval chasing. Keep helping colleagues make clear requests and resolve legitimate exceptions.
lenses.options: Show requester-supplied quotes side by side and flag differences in total cost or terms. For expenses, explain permitted correction routes using the approved policy.
lenses.altitude: Maintain request templates, policy checks and approval routing. Monitor where submissions fail and improve instructions.
reach: Prepare commitment data for FP&A.
Support site buyers with complete order documentation.
Prepare expense reimbursement inputs for Payroll where the approved process requires them.

tasks.human_edge: Judge the business purpose, supplier suitability and legitimate policy exceptions while respecting the employee's circumstances.
tasks.pattern_why: Requests and receipts require extraction, policy lookup, draft preparation and routing across systems. A person approves the commitment or reimbursement before it becomes effective.

in_practice.trigger: A purchase request or expense claim is submitted through the designated intake.
steps: Extract requested items or receipt fields and preserve references to the source.
Check completeness, duplicates, approved supplier status and applicable policy rules.
Prepare the order or expense report with site coding and any exception highlighted.
Route the pack to the authorised budget holder or expense approver.
After approval, create or release the authorised record and retain the approval evidence.
in_practice.human_gate: The authorised budget holder approves purchase commitments and the designated manager approves expenses. Payroll resolves taxable reimbursement treatment; supplier bank changes follow separate controls.
systems: AFAS purchase workflow if licensed and configured
data_needed: Purchase requests, quotes and receipts
Approved supplier and employee records
Expense policy and current approval matrix
Site codes and available budget information
Approved reimbursement treatment and duplicate history
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS order or expense dossier and a restricted intake register with source references, policy version, approval trail and resulting record identifier.

evidence.claim: AFAS provides purchase-order workflows that route orders to designated reviewers such as budget holders; Noordhaven's access to this workflow needs confirmation.
Preparing request packs from receipts and approved policies is plausible; the 50% handling reduction and 1.5-fold speedup are untested estimates.

risks: A draft order could be sent before approval and create an unintended commitment.
Outdated policies or approval limits can route requests incorrectly.
Receipts can contain unnecessary personal details; restrict storage and model access under AVG/GDPR.
The assistant must not decide taxable reimbursement treatment or reject employee claims solely on a model judgement.
research_questions: Which purchase and expense workflows are already available in Noordhaven's AFAS licence?
Are policies and approval limits current, explicit and consistent across all three sites?
How much elapsed time comes from document preparation versus waiting for approvers?
Does a pilot produce complete packs faster without increasing unauthorised orders or incorrect reimbursements?

role.altitude: The bookkeeper becomes the owner of routine transaction controls and exception resolution: maintaining mappings, proving completeness and improving the handoffs that delay close.
reach: Prepare recurring journals and reconciliation packs for the Accountant.
Provide payment allocation and billing evidence to the Credit and Collections Officer.
Maintain received-but-not-invoiced, unbilled-service and purchase-commitment schedules for the Controller and FP&A.
Support the Payroll Specialist with input completeness and finance reconciliation, within restricted access.
Help site buyers and agency contacts improve orders, receipts and invoice references.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks total 411.9 hours per FTE annually, about 25.7% of the supplied role-time baseline, or 1,235.7 hours across three FTE. Today workflows are assumptions to validate. Savings are untested reductions in human handling; speedup estimates refer to elapsed completion time including automated work, review and expected waiting. Do not add overlapping savings from invoice matching, coding, arithmetic and journal transfer. Existing AFAS automation, maintenance effort, missing operational data and approval waits constrain the gain. At EUR 45/hour, released time represents capacity value rather than automatic cash savings. Accounting policy, payroll approval, commercial disputes and payment authorisation remain with the accountable people.
skills_to_grow: Configure and assess AFAS native workflows before commissioning custom automation.
Write explicit matching, coding and validation rules.
Trace transactions from source evidence through approval to the ledger.
Investigate exceptions and improve upstream data quality.
Assess document extraction using representative errors and reviewer corrections.
Apply AVG/GDPR access controls and recognise when employee-data changes require OR involvement.
Measure handling time, elapsed time, incorrect postings and ongoing maintenance separately.
role.ambitious_version: Run a daily transaction-quality service across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Surface missing receipts, agency rate differences, unbilled services, unresolved cash allocations and late journals early enough for owners to act before close. Give the Controller and FP&A reconciled actuals and commitments with clear source timestamps; the nightly Power BI refresh remains a reporting view, while operational checks use current AFAS data. Judge success by fewer days to close with a trusted forecast, lower DSO, more invoices processed without touch and fewer audit adjustments.
